questions.prompt: Which sentence is written in the passive voice?
choices: The cake was eaten by the children.
The children are eating the cake.
The children will eat the cake.
answers: The cake was eaten by the children.
questions.explanation: In the passive, the thing the action happens to (the cake) comes first, followed by was eaten.

questions.prompt: Rewrite in the passive voice: The dog chased the cat.
answers: The cat was chased by the dog.
questions.explanation: Move the cat to the front and use was chased: The cat was chased by the dog.

questions.prompt: Which verb form completes the passive sentence? The letters ___ this morning.
questions.explanation: The passive uses a form of be with the past participle: were delivered.
questions.audioText: Which verb form completes the passive sentence? The letters blank this morning.

questions.prompt: Is this sentence active or passive? The window was smashed during the storm.
questions.explanation: The window had the action done to it, and we use was smashed, so it is passive.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the subjunctive form?
choices: If I were taller, I could reach the shelf.
If I was taller, I could reach the shelf.
I am taller than the shelf.
When I am taller, I will reach the shelf.
answers: If I were taller, I could reach the shelf.
questions.explanation: If I were is the subjunctive. It is used for things that are imagined or wished for.

questions.prompt: The head teacher insists that every pupil ___ on time.
questions.explanation: After insists that, formal writing uses the subjunctive be.
questions.audioText: The head teacher insists that every pupil blank on time.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence in the subjunctive: If he ___ here, he would help us.
questions.explanation: If he were here is the subjunctive, because he is not really here.
questions.audioText: Complete the sentence in the subjunctive: If he blank here, he would help us.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the most formal?
choices: Just ask if you need help.
Give us a shout if you need a hand.
questions.explanation: Request, assistance and required are formal words, and there are no contractions or slang.

questions.prompt: Which is the formal way to write: The kids got loads of prizes.
choices: The kids got lots of prizes.
The kids won loads of prizes.
The children got loads of prizes.
questions.explanation: Children, received and many are more formal than kids, got and loads.

questions.prompt: Which word is the formal synonym for find out?
questions.explanation: Discover is a formal verb that means find out.

questions.prompt: Which word is a synonym of enormous?
questions.explanation: Huge means nearly the same as enormous, so it is a synonym.

questions.prompt: Which word is an antonym of generous?
questions.explanation: Selfish means the opposite of generous, so it is an antonym.

questions.prompt: Tick the two words that are synonyms of brave.
questions.explanation: Courageous and fearless mean nearly the same as brave. Timid and nervous are antonyms.

questions.prompt: Which word is an antonym of ancient?
questions.explanation: Modern is the opposite of ancient.

questions.prompt: Tap where the semi-colon should go.
questions.explanation: It was late and the streets were empty could each be a sentence, so a semi-colon joins them: It was late; the streets were empty.
questions.audioText: It was late the streets were empty. Tap where the semi-colon should go.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a semi-colon correctly?
choices: I love reading; my brother prefers films.
I love; reading my brother prefers films.
I love reading my; brother prefers films.
I; love reading my brother prefers films.
answers: I love reading; my brother prefers films.
questions.explanation: The semi-colon goes between two main clauses that are closely linked.

questions.prompt: Tap where the semi-colon should go.
questions.explanation: The sun came out; we went to the beach. Both parts are main clauses.
questions.audioText: The sun came out we went to the beach. Tap where the semi-colon should go.

questions.prompt: Tap where the colon should go.
questions.explanation: The colon introduces the list and comes after the full sentence You will need three things.
questions.audioText: You will need three things a pencil, a ruler and a rubber. Tap where the colon should go.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
choices: The match was cancelled: the pitch was flooded.
The match: was cancelled the pitch was flooded.
The: match was cancelled the pitch was flooded.
The match was: cancelled the pitch was flooded.
answers: The match was cancelled: the pitch was flooded.
questions.explanation: The colon comes after a main clause and introduces the explanation.

questions.prompt: Why is a colon used here? Mia was delighted: she had won first prize.
choices: to separate items in a list
questions.explanation: The second part explains why Mia was delighted.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a hyphen to show the shark eats people?
choices: We saw a man eating shark.
questions.explanation: Man-eating is one describing word, so the hyphen shows the shark eats men. Without it, it sounds like a man is eating a shark.

questions.prompt: Which word needs a hyphen to mean cover again?
questions.explanation: Recover means get better. Re-cover means cover again, so the hyphen changes the meaning.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a hyphen correctly?
choices: My sister is a well-known author.
My sister is a well known-author.
My sister-is a well known author.
My-sister is a well known author.
answers: My sister is a well-known author.
questions.explanation: Well-known is a compound adjective describing author, so it is joined with a hyphen.

questions.prompt: What word class is the underlined word? We watched the match after school.
questions.explanation: After is followed by a noun (school), not a clause, so here it is a preposition.

questions.prompt: What word class is the underlined word? The water was calm.
questions.explanation: Calm describes the water, so here it is an adjective.

questions.prompt: What word class is the underlined word? Please calm the puppy down.
questions.explanation: Here calm is something you do, so it is a verb. The same word can belong to different word classes.

questions.prompt: Tick the two determiners: Those children ate every biscuit.
questions.explanation: Those and every come before nouns and tell us which or how many, so they are determiners.

questions.prompt: What word class is the underlined word? She sang beautifully.
questions.explanation: Beautifully tells us how she sang, so it is an adverb.

questions.prompt: Which part is the subordinate clause? Although it was raining, we played outside.
questions.explanation: Although it was raining does not make sense on its own, so it is the subordinate clause.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a main clause?
questions.explanation: The bell rang makes sense on its own. The others start with a subordinating conjunction.

questions.prompt: Tick the two subordinating conjunctions.
questions.explanation: Because and unless start subordinate clauses. And and but are coordinating conjunctions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a subordinate clause?
choices: We left early so that we could get seats.
We left early and got seats.
We left early, but it was busy.
answers: We left early so that we could get seats.
questions.explanation: So that we could get seats is a subordinate clause. It does not make sense on its own.
